tdd_steps.implementation: Implement TokenRateKind, PricingRate, and PricingTable::seed() seeding claude-3-5-sonnet, claude-3-5-haiku, and qwen-2.5-coder rows carrying forward the exact dollar amounts from CRIT-LUMEN-002/003/004 unchanged, each row's effective_from set to a shared baseline epoch constant with effective_until None. Implement PricingTable::rate_for with the CRIT-LUMEN-008 branch: when the requested model string matches no row at all, fall back to claude-3-5-sonnet's rate for the requested kind/as_of.

tasks.title: Token Economics Zero-Division, Savings Clamping, Percentage-Scale & Prompt Summation Tests via Per-Turn TurnPricingInput

tdd_steps.failing_test: Add test_token_economics_zero_division_clamping_and_scale with five assertions against TokenEconomics::calculate(turns: &[TurnPricingInput], model_name, pricing: &PricingTable, provided_cost_usd: Option<f64>): (a) calculate(&[], "claude-3-5-sonnet", &pricing, None) asserts cache_hit_ratio == 0.0, efficiency_multiplier == 1.0, total_cost_usd == 0.0 (CRIT-007); (b) a single TurnPricingInput whose input/cache_creation/cache_read token counts are chosen so cache_read_tokens is exactly half of (input+cache_creation+cache_read) asserts cache_hit_ratio == 50.0 (not 0.5), locking in the 0-100 percentage scale (CRIT-005); (c) a turn with zero cache activity asserts net_savings_usd == 0.0 (never negative) even though baseline_cost_no_cache_usd == total_cost_usd in that case (CRIT-009); (d) TurnTokenUsage::prompt_tokens on a fixture with distinct input/cache_creation/cache_read values asserts it equals their sum (CRIT-010); (e) a mixed-cache turn asserts efficiency_multiplier == baseline_cost_no_cache_usd / total_cost_usd (CRIT-006).
tdd_steps.expected_failure: Fails to compile: TokenEconomics::calculate's prior signature took pre-summed session totals directly, not a &[TurnPricingInput] slice plus &PricingTable and provided_cost_usd parameters.
tdd_steps.implementation: Define TurnPricingInput { usage: TurnTokenUsage, timestamp: DateTime<Utc>, tier: Option<CompactString> } in crates/lumen-model/src/economics.rs (co-located with TokenEconomics, which consumes it). Change TokenEconomics::calculate to accept turns: &[TurnPricingInput], model_name: &str, pricing: &PricingTable, provided_cost_usd: Option<f64>. For each turn, price it via PricingTable::rate_for(model_name, turn.tier.as_deref(), kind, turn.timestamp) per TokenRateKind and sum the per-turn costs into total_cost_usd; sum raw input_tokens/output_tokens/cache_creation_tokens/cache_read_tokens as simple totals across turns (unaffected by the pricing change). Guard cache_hit_ratio/efficiency_multiplier against zero total prompt tokens, and clamp net_savings_usd to a minimum of 0.0.

tasks.title: PricingTable::rate_for Versioned As-Of Lookup and Deterministic Tie-Break Tests

tdd_steps.failing_test: Add test_rate_for_versioned_lookup_and_tie_break with three scenarios against a hand-built PricingTable (not PricingTable::seed()): (a) two rows for the same (model, tier, kind) with non-overlapping consecutive [effective_from, effective_until) windows representing a price change -- rate_for with an as_of inside the first window returns the first rate, and with an as_of inside the second window returns the second rate, proving the CALLING TURN's own timestamp (not wall-clock now) selects the row; (b) two rows with identical effective_from and no effective_until (an authoring-error overlap) -- rate_for returns the rate of whichever row appears LAST in PricingTable.rates' vector declaration order; (c) two rows with different effective_from values whose windows overlap -- rate_for returns the row with the LATER effective_from.
tdd_steps.expected_failure: Fails to compile or fails scenario (b)/(c): rate_for does not exist yet, or an initial naive linear-scan implementation returns the FIRST matching row instead of applying the effective_from-then-declaration-order tie-break.
tdd_steps.implementation: Implement PricingTable::rate_for to filter rows by (model, tier, kind) and by as_of within [effective_from, effective_until) (effective_until == None treated as unbounded), then among matches select by maximum effective_from, breaking ties by the LATEST index in PricingTable.rates.
tdd_steps.expected_pass: test_rate_for_versioned_lookup_and_tie_break passes for all three window/tie-break scenarios (a)-(c).

tasks.title: Recognized-Model Missing-Rate-Kind Returns 0.0, Not Sonnet Fallback

tdd_steps.failing_test: Add test_recognized_model_missing_kind_returns_zero: build a PricingTable seeded with qwen-2.5-coder rows for Input/CacheRead/Output only (no CacheWrite row, matching CRIT-LUMEN-004's real gap -- Qwen has no seeded cache-write price), call rate_for("qwen-2.5-coder", None, TokenRateKind::CacheWrite, as_of) and assert it returns exactly 0.0, and explicitly assert the result is NOT equal to claude-3-5-sonnet's $3.75/M CacheWrite rate -- distinguishing this recognized-model/missing-kind case from the CRIT-LUMEN-008 unrecognized-model fallback path covered in TASK-MODEL-001.
tdd_steps.expected_failure: Fails if rate_for falls back to Sonnet's (or any other model's) CacheWrite rate for a recognized model's genuinely-absent rate kind, or if it panics instead of returning 0.0.
tdd_steps.implementation: In PricingTable::rate_for, first check whether the model string matches at least one row at all (recognized). If recognized, search only that model's rows for the requested (tier, kind, as_of); if none match, return 0.0 directly without falling through to the CRIT-LUMEN-008 unrecognized-model-wide fallback branch, which only triggers when the model matches zero rows.
tdd_steps.expected_pass: test_recognized_model_missing_kind_returns_zero passes, confirming 0.0 is returned and no other model's rate is substituted.
